title: Computer fundamentals
description: Six original sample questions to try your study desk. This is a demonstration, not an official certification exam.

questions.prompt: An application needs the IP address associated with a domain name. Which service provides this lookup?

options.explanation: The Domain Name System provides records used to resolve names to IP addresses.
DHCP supplies network configuration to clients, including IP addresses and DNS server settings.
TLS protects communication through authentication and encryption.
The Network Time Protocol synchronizes clocks.

questions.explanation: DNS resolves names. Other protocols may configure the connection or protect the traffic, but they do not perform this name lookup.

questions.prompt: A database operation must update two records together. If either update fails, neither change should remain. Which feature provides this behavior?

options.explanation: Atomicity ensures all operations in a transaction succeed together or are rolled back.
An index can accelerate lookups; it does not make multiple updates atomic.
Caching reuses results and does not provide atomic updates.
ORDER BY controls result ordering.

questions.explanation: Use a transaction to group related changes into one atomic unit of work.

options.explanation: JSON uses quoted property names and supports boolean values.
A JSON document can be an array.
JSON property names must use double quotes.
JSON does not allow trailing commas.

questions.explanation: JSON supports objects and arrays. Its syntax is stricter than JavaScript object literals.

questions.prompt: Which component normally stores a running program's working data and loses its contents when power is removed?

options.explanation: Ordinary system RAM is volatile memory.
An SSD provides persistent storage.
A hard disk retains data without power.
Read-only memory is nonvolatile.

questions.explanation: Working memory and persistent storage have different roles. RAM is fast, temporary working space.

questions.prompt: In Git, what does a **commit** represent?

options.text: A recorded project snapshot with metadata and parent references
options.explanation: A commit identifies a tree and includes metadata such as the author and message.

options.text: An automatic upload to a remote server
options.explanation: A commit can be created locally. Pushing transfers commits to a remote.

options.text: The deletion of all previous versions
options.explanation: A normal commit extends history rather than deleting earlier commits.

options.text: A permanently separate copy of the entire repository
options.explanation: Branches are references to commits, not permanently independent repository copies.

questions.explanation: Committing records a state of the project in local history. Uploading it is a separate operation.

questions.prompt: Which two HTTP methods are defined as **safe**, meaning their intended semantics are read-only?

options.explanation: GET retrieves a representation and has safe semantics.
HEAD requests response headers without the response body and has safe semantics.
POST can cause state changes and is not defined as safe.
DELETE requests removal and is not defined as safe.

questions.explanation: Safe describes the requested semantics. Servers can still perform incidental actions such as logging.
